paper_title: Joint Detection of Fraud and Concept Drift inOnline Conversations with   LLM-Assisted Judgment
caption: A runtime comparison between our ensemble model and various LLM models on the SEconvo dataset
model_annotation: The bar chart titled "Runtime Comparison of Models in Streaming Environment" presents a comparison of runtime performance (in seconds) between "Our Joint Framework" and several large language models (LLMs) on the SEconvo dataset. The horizontal axis lists the model categories: "Our Joint Framework," "ChatGPT," "DeepSeek," "LLaMA," and "Claude," arranged from left to right. The vertical axis represents runtime in seconds, ranging from 0 to 400 with major gridlines at intervals of 50. A legend indicates that dark green bars correspond to "Our Joint Framework" and light blue bars to "LLM Models." The chart displays a single dark green bar for "Our Joint Framework" with a value of 77 seconds, which is significantly lower than all other models. The light blue bars represent the LLMs: ChatGPT (190 seconds), DeepSeek (365 seconds), LLaMA (172 seconds), and Claude (243 seconds). Each bar is labeled with its exact runtime value above it. The data is presented in a straightforward grouped bar format, with each model category having one bar (except for "Our Joint Framework," which is the sole representative of its category), and the bars are not stacked. The chart visually emphasizes the superior runtime efficiency of the proposed joint framework compared to the individual LLMs, with DeepSeek exhibiting the longest runtime and LLaMA the shortest among the LLMs.
